# Two-sample t-test power calculation
# H0: μ_treatment = μ_control vs H1: μ_treatment > μ_control (one-sided)
# Parameters:
# - Effect size (difference in means): 4.3 dBA
# - Common SD: 7.8 dBA
# - Sample size per group: 32
# - Alpha: 0.05 (one-sided)

# Load required package
library(stats)

# Define parameters
delta <- 4.3          # expected difference in means (dBA)
sigma <- 7.8          # common standard deviation (dBA)
n_per_group <- 32     # sample size per group
alpha <- 0.05         # significance level (one-sided)

# Calculate Cohen's d (standardized effect size)
cohens_d <- delta / sigma

# For a two-sample t-test with equal sample sizes n per group:
# - Total degrees of freedom: df = 2n - 2 = 2(32) - 2 = 62
# - Non-centrality parameter: lambda = (delta / sigma) * sqrt(n / 2)
# where the factor sqrt(n/2) comes from the SE of the difference: SE = sigma * sqrt(2/n)
# so t-stat = (delta / SE) = delta / (sigma * sqrt(2/n)) = (delta/sigma) * sqrt(n/2)

df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
lambda <- cohens_d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)

# Critical value for one-sided test at alpha = 0.05
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df = df)

# Power: P(T > t_crit) under H1, where T ~ t(df, lambda)
power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df = df, ncp = lambda)

# Display results

cat("=====================================\n\n")

library(jsonlite)

# Input parameters from the candidate answer
delta <- 4.3          # expected difference in means (dBA)
sigma <- 7.8          # common standard deviation (dBA)
n_per_group <- 32     # sample size per group
alpha <- 0.05         # significance level (one-sided)

# ============================================================================
# ANALYTICAL VERIFICATION: Non-centrality parameter approach
# ============================================================================

cat("INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION\n")
cat("========================\n\n")

# For a one-sided pooled t-test:
# Under H0: μ1 = μ2, the test statistic is t = (Y1-bar - Y2-bar) / SE_pooled
# where SE_pooled = sqrt(2*s_p^2/n) and s_p^2 is the pooled variance estimate
# Under H1 with true difference delta, E[Y1-bar - Y2-bar] = delta
# The non-centrality parameter λ = delta / SE_theoretical = delta / (sigma * sqrt(2/n))
# This simplifies to λ = (delta/sigma) * sqrt(n/2)

df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
cohens_d <- delta / sigma
se_difference <- sigma * sqrt(2 / n_per_group)
lambda <- delta / se_difference  # Alternative formulation

cat("1. ANALYTICAL CALCULATION (Non-centrality approach):\n")
cat(sprintf("   Degrees of freedom: df = 2n - 2 = %d\n", df))
cat(sprintf("   Standard error of difference: SE = sigma*sqrt(2/n) = %.6f\n", se_difference))
cat(sprintf("   Non-centrality parameter: λ = delta/SE = %.6f\n", lambda))
cat(sprintf("   Equivalently: λ = (delta/sigma)*sqrt(n/2) = %.6f\n", cohens_d * sqrt(n_per_group/2)))

# Critical value
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df = df)
cat(sprintf("   Critical t-value (one-sided, α=0.05): t_crit = %.6f\n", t_crit))

# Power calculation
power_analytical <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df = df, ncp = lambda)
cat(sprintf("   Power = P(T > %.6f | df=%d, λ=%.6f) = %.10f\n\n", 
            t_crit, df, lambda, power_analytical))

# ============================================================================
# MONTE CARLO VERIFICATION: Simulate data and perform t-tests
# ============================================================================

cat("2. MONTE CARLO VERIFICATION (10,000 simulations):\n")

set.seed(42)
n_sims <- 10000

# Arrays to store results
t_stats <- numeric(n_sims)
p_values <- numeric(n_sims)
reject_count <- 0

for (i in 1:n_sims) {
  # Generate data under H1 (true difference = delta, equal variances = sigma^2)
  group1 <- rnorm(n_per_group, mean = 0, sd = sigma)
  group2 <- rnorm(n_per_group, mean = delta, sd = sigma)
  
  # Conduct one-sided pooled t-test: H1: μ2 > μ1
  # t.test with alternative="greater" tests μ2 > μ1
  result <- t.test(group2, group1, 
                   var.equal = TRUE,           # Use pooled variance
                   alternative = "greater",     # One-sided test
                   mu = 0)
  
  p_values[i] <- result$p.value
  t_stats[i] <- result$statistic
  
  # Reject if p < alpha
  if (result$p.value < alpha) {
    reject_count <- reject_count + 1
  }
}

ci_mc_upper <- power_mc + 1.96 * se_mc

cat(sprintf("   Standard error (MC): %.6f\n", se_mc))

# ============================================================================

set.seed(43)
n_sims_null <- 10000
reject_null <- 0

    reject_null <- reject_null + 1
  }
}

cat(sprintf("   Type I error rate (H0): %.10f\n", type_i_error))
cat(sprintf("   Expected (nominal α):   0.05\n")
cat(sprintf("   SE (under H0):          %.6f\n\n",

# - Common SD: 7.8 dBA
# - Sample size per group: 32

sigma <- 7.8          # common standard deviation (dBA)
n_per_group <- 32     # sample size per group
alpha <- 0.05         # significance level (one-sided)

# Calculate Cohen's d (standardized effect size)
cohens_d <- delta / sigma

# For a two-sample t-test with equal sample sizes n per group:
# - Total degrees of freedom: df = 2n - 2 = 2(32) - 2 = 62
# - Non-centrality parameter: lambda = (delta / sigma) * sqrt(n / 2)
# where the factor sqrt(n/2) comes from the SE of the difference: SE = sigma * sqrt(2/n)
# so t-stat = (delta / SE) = delta / (sigma * sqrt(2/n)) = (delta/sigma) * sqrt(n/2)
